headline: Senior Greens figures say new leadership must stop Labor approving fossil fuel projects ‘by whatever means’

members.title: Senior Greens figures say new leadership must stop Labor approving fossil fuel projects ‘by whatever means’
members.lead: No excuses for next leader of party, Adam Bandt says, while Bob Brown warns they must also be able to take on Pauline Hanson and One Nation Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The former Greens leader Adam Bandt says the party’s new leadership team, which could be chosen as early as today, will face mounting pressure from grassroots members to block the Albanese government from approving any new coal and gas projects “by whatever means”. He told Guardian Australia there would be no excuses for the new leader, likely to be elected at a two-day retreat in Sydney which begins today, to allow Labor to approve any new fossil fuel development. members.title: David Shoebridge launches leadership bid ahead of Greens ballot at party retreat
members.lead: Shoebridge to stand on a joint ticket with Steph Hodgins-May – a first-term senator from Victoria Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast New South Wales senator David Shoebridge has joined the race to become the Greens’ new leader, with an increasingly crowded field revealing splits among the 11-member party room. Shoebridge said on Wednesday morning he would stand on a joint ticket with Victorian senator Steph Hodgins-May as his proposed deputy, facing off with the deputy leader, Mehreen Faruqi, and communications spokesperson, Sarah Hanson-Young.
